clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old male with a history of cryptorchidism treated surgically in childhood presented with a 1-year history of left scrotal swelling, recently complicated by local hyperemia and pain. Physical examination revealed a 6/15 cm hard, intensely painful left testicular mass with inflamed adjacent tissues. Laboratory workup showed elevated inflammatory markers (WBC 16500/dl, ESR 74 mm/h, fibrinogen 1084 mg/dl, ALP 937 UI/l). Ultrasound imaging demonstrated structural modifications of the left testis characteristic of testicular malignancy with no regional adenopathies. Radical inguinal orchiectomy was performed with an uneventful postoperative course. Histopathologic examination of the orchiectomy specimen confirmed seminoma with cribriform and pseudoglandular pattern. The tumor measured 6/15 cm (≥4 cm), meeting T2 size criteria. No regional adenopathies were identified on ultrasound, supporting N0 staging. The patient was referred to oncology for further treatment.
